conversation: Good to see everyone. My family’s fished this lake for years, and I want it to keep supporting our village. With 100 tons in the lake, we can catch 50 tons total and leave 50 to double back to 100 next month. How about we each take 10 tons this month? That’s $10,000 apiece, and we can keep earning that each month if we stick to the limit. Let’s check our catches together afterward. John, what do you think?

I’m on board, Luke. My family taught me to leave enough fish for the next season, and a 10-ton share each gives all five families a steady income. Let’s agree that 50 tons is our combined limit, not a target anyone can exceed by taking someone else’s share. John, can you commit to that?

Count me in for 10 tons. I learned to fish here with my family, and I want our village’s children to have that same chance. Let’s also agree that if the lake ever starts a month below 100 tons, we’ll review our shares before fishing so we still leave enough to replenish it. John, can you join us on those terms?

I’m in—10 tons for me, with our combined catch capped at 50. My family taught me that a good catch isn’t worth much if there’s nothing left for next month. I also agree we should review our shares before fishing if stocks fall below 100 tons. Jack, are you comfortable committing to the same limits?

I’m comfortable with that—10 tons for me and no more than 50 between us. This lake has supported my family for generations, and keeping it healthy means steady work for the village. We’ve all agreed, so let’s stick to our shares this month, compare catches afterward, and review the stock before fishing next month.
